html:
Sango is the language spoken by nearly everyone in the Central African Republic, a trade language that grew along the Ubangi river and was made the national language in 1964.

It is based on the language of the Ngbandi people, with many words from French. Traders, soldiers and missionaries spread it along the river in colonial times, and it became the common tongue of Ubangi-Shari, used by Catholic and Protestant missions to preach.

In 1991 it became an official language alongside French. Unlike most African states, the country has one African language almost all its people share, used in Bangui markets and on radio. It is one of the few creole-based national languages in Africa.
sum: Sango is the language spoken by nearly everyone in the Central African Republic, a trade language that grew along the Ubangi river and was made the national language in 1964.
